reasons: Status is 'compliant' with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output; the cited paragraphs support it — there is no 'automatically renew' or 'unless notice ... days prior' mechanic anywhere in the quoted text.

The maintenance term is a 'renewable one-year term' (12 months, extendable only by affirmative agreement) and the licence is perpetual subject to fee payment, which matches the preferred position of renewal by mutual written agreement with a 12-month term.

The failed deterministic check (value=90) keys off the ninety (90) day figure in p0118, which is Sparkling's (our) termination-for-convenience notice period, not a non-renewal notice window; it is a customer exit right and belongs to a termination rule, so the heuristic is a false positive here.

The two shortfalls the rationale identifies (no CPI/3% uplift cap on renewal-period maintenance fees, no vendor renewal reminder) are minor sub-elements properly noted in the rationale rather than redlined, consistent with the classification semantics.
